September 6, 2026

Fifth Circuit rules Constitution guarantees no right to clean drinking water

tags: legal, politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals has ruled that the Constitution does not guarantee a right to clean drinking water or a right to accurate information from public officials. The case arose from Jackson, Mississippi, where residents sued after learning their drinking water was contaminated with lead; a lower court dismissed the suit and the residents appealed on due process grounds. Writing for the majority, Judge Kurt Engelhardt, a Trump appointee, held that the Constitution does not guarantee redress for every government wrongdoing, and said residents dissatisfied with their water should elect officials who would change it.

ICE granted court permission for non-consensual feeding tube surgery on detainee

tags: immigration, legal, health
sources: @aaronparnas

A federal court this week granted ICE permission to perform a non-consensual surgical procedure to insert a gastric tube into the abdomen of an undocumented immigrant on hunger strike, according to The Guardian. It is not confirmed whether the procedure has taken place; ICE has until mid-September, and the man reportedly has no legal representation. Force-feeding of detainees has occurred in more than a dozen confirmed cases in detention centers over the past 18 months, but surgical insertion of a gastric tube for this purpose has not previously been reported. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas is representing ICE.

Trump order strips endangered species protections from gray wolves

tags: environment, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump has signed an executive order removing endangered species protections from gray wolves, including the Mexican gray wolf subspecies, with the effect of allowing them to be killed in the United States. The order is framed as assistance to ranchers who say the wolves prey on livestock. Environmental advocates warn it could derail long-term recovery efforts. About 300 Mexican gray wolves remain in the United States, alongside more than 18,000 gray wolves.

Trump officials draft plan to pay stay-at-home parents with working parents' child care funds

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration is drafting a rule to pay stay-at-home parents using a Department of Health and Human Services fund created in the 1990s to help low-income and working-class parents afford child care, according to the New York Times. The proposal, described as a top agenda item for Vice President JD Vance, would apply only to married couples within certain income brackets where one parent stays home, and involves subsidies of roughly $9,000 a year per child. Redirecting the money would reduce funds available to working parents and child care providers, which could raise child care rates. The change would be made through executive rulemaking and would not require congressional approval.

Labor Day gas prices hit record high

tags: markets, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Gas prices in the United States will reach a record high for Labor Day, according to AAA, with the national average at $4.15 per gallon — the highest ever recorded for the holiday and about 95 cents more than a year ago. Diesel has also surged, reaching $5.90 per gallon, more than $2 above its level at this time last year. Relief is not expected in the near term, with the war potentially continuing for six months or more.

Walmart privacy policy discloses biometric and behavioral data collection

tags: surveillance, privacy, tech
sources: @ericmoutsos

Walmart has updated its privacy policy to disclose the categories of customer information it collects, including names, email and shipping addresses, IP addresses, social media information, browsing and search activity, keystroke patterns, household income, education, employment and family health information. The policy also lists voice prints, iris and retina imagery, face geometry, palm prints and fingerprints, along with device location, criminal history and background checks. The company says it may draw inferences about customers from their preferences, characteristics and shopping behavior, and that it uses automated license plate readers, in-store surveillance cameras, in-store wifi and Bluetooth to detect the location of customers' mobile devices. The disclosure has been linked to Walmart's rollout of Bluetooth-enabled digital shelf price tags across all its stores by the end of 2026, which allow prices to be updated in real time.

Pentagon guidance adds menstrual cycle screening for female service members

tags: defence, health, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Pentagon has issued new health guidance that includes screening female service members for changes in their menstrual cycles. The measure is part of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's broader "Health and Human Performance Optimization" initiative.

US cut Nepal landslide monitoring program a year before deadly floods

tags: climate, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The United States cut funding in January 2025 for a long-running natural hazards program that identified and monitored landslide hotspots in Nepal, CNN has confirmed, a year before floods on the Nepal-Tibet border killed hundreds and left others missing. The program, Project SERVIR Hindu Kush Himalaya, aimed to map areas prone to landslides and other risks made more common by climate change. The cut halted work to improve landslide situational awareness and was made as part of the Trump administration's reduction of foreign aid. The program would not necessarily have prevented the recent disaster but was intended as a first step toward future protections.
